def: The culture of ancient Egypt has fascinated outsiders from its own day well into the modern day, long after that culture was subsumed first by Greco-Roman, then Christian, then Muslim currents.

c: The increasing power and wealth of the kings during the early dynastic period was reflected in their elaborate mastaba tombs and mortuary cult structures at Abydos, which were used to celebrate the…
def: A mastaba is a type of ancient Egyptian tomb in the form of a flat-roofed, rectangular structure with inward sloping sides, constructed out of mudbricks or limestone.

c: As the power of the kings diminished, regional governors called nomarchs began to challenge the supremacy of the office of king.
def: A nomarch was a provincial governor in ancient Egypt; the country was divided into 42 provinces, called nomes.

c: In the Early Dynastic Period, which began about 3000 BC, the first of the Dynastic kings solidified control over Lower Egypt by establishing a capital at Memphis, from which he could control the…
def: A trade route is a logistical network identified as a series of pathways and stoppages used for the commercial transport of cargo.

c: The relief and portrait sculpture of the period captured subtle, individual details that reached new heights of technical sophistication.
def: Relief is a sculptural method in which the sculpted pieces remain attached to a solid background of the same material.

c: Some traditions merged, as Greek and Egyptian gods were syncretized into composite deities, such as Serapis, and classical Greek forms of sculpture influenced traditional Egyptian motifs.
def: Egyptian mythology is the collection of myths from ancient Egypt, which describe the actions of the Egyptian gods as a means of understanding the world around them.

c: Beginning in the New Kingdom, oracles played a major role in the legal system, dispensing justice in both civil and criminal cases.
def: An oracle is a person or thing considered to provide insight, wise counsel or prophetic predictions, most notably including precognition of the future, inspired by deities.

c: Prayers were made to the goddess Isis. Moldy bread, honey, and copper salts were also used to prevent infection from dirt in burns.
def: Isis was a major goddess in ancient Egyptian religion whose worship spread throughout the Greco-Roman world.
